entry.why: A per-user cap keeps one signed-in client from overloading the service or crowding out others. A fixed clock-minute window is simple to implement and predictable, and Retry-After tells clients exactly when to retry. Writing nothing on a rejected request means throttled calls have no side effects and are safe to retry.
entry.tradeoff: Fixed windows are cheap and easy to reason about but allow bursts across a window boundary (up to 240 requests in a short span). Legitimate heavy clients may hit 429s, and batch or sync requests are the way to do more work per request.
entry.author: llm:sonnet
